title: Demand-shaped Budgeting and Burn Trigger Framework
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines a demand-shaped budgeting process and an associated set of burn triggers for Redwood Inference. The goal is to align procurement, contract commitments, and revenue recognition assumptions with leading indicators (usage, model mix, and committed capacity) and to specify deterministic actions when financial or operational thresholds are crossed.

Scope: Applies to Finance, Product, and Platform procurement owners for hosted API, Dedicated capacity contracts, and Private deployments. It covers quarterly budget reforecasts, mid-quarter trigger evaluation, procurement hold rules, and billing/revrec coordination when triggers fire.

Key definitions

- Burn: Net cash spend against the operating budget (monthly run-rate).
- Demand signals: API requests per minute (RPM), average tokens per call, and percentage of requests routed to lower-cost model variants.
- Commitment window: Customer reserved capacity agreements (monthly/annual), and expected uplift windows.
- Trigger event: A predefined condition that requires an operational or financial action (e.g., pause non-essential procurement).

High-level principles

1) Forward-looking, signal-driven decisions: Budget adjustments should be driven by measurable signals (usage, model mix, churn) and contractual levers (commitments, repricing windows).
2) Clear separation of responsibilities: Finance owns thresholds and decisions for customer-facing commitments; Platform/Product owns operational mitigations (routing, autoscale).
3) Minimize customer disruption: When actions affect customers, prefer non-breaking mitigations first (e.g., route to compatible model variant, apply temporary rate-limits) and notify CS & account teams immediately.

Demand signals and thresholds

We use three tiers of signals: Leading (L), Primary (P), and Confirming (C). Triggers must follow the sequence: L -> P -> C within the evaluation window to be actionable.

- L: 14-day moving average of RPM vs plan; threshold: +/- 12% deviation (increase or decrease).
- P: 30-day revenue-weighted usage vs plan; threshold: +/- 8% deviation.
- C: Contracted committed-capacity delta (net new or churn) over 60 days: >= 10% change.

Burn trigger matrix (summary)

| Trigger name | Condition (Sequence) | Immediate finance action | Operational mitigation | Customer impact | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Green (monitor) | L only | Log & notify | No action | None | Finance/Platform |
| Yellow (prepare) | L + P | Prepare reforecast; procurement hold advisory | Increase caching, prioritize batching | Low (rate-limit advisory) | Finance/Product |
| Red (action) | L + P + C | Execute procurement pause; engage exec review; revise revenue recognition assumptions | Canary rollback of recent rollouts; strict rate limiting | Medium (possible temporary throttling and throttled SLAs) | CFO + Head of Platform |
| Critical (escalate) | Red persisted 30 days or sudden >20% negative deviation | Activate contingency fund; contract renegotiation roadmap | Emergency cost-shedding (suspend non-critical routes) | High (customer T&Cs may be affected) | CFO + CEO + Legal |

Procedure: evaluation cadence and responsibilities

1) Daily automated ingestion: Metrics (RPM, tokens/call), billing estimates, and committed-capacity events flow into the Budget Signals dashboard (owned by Finance Ops).
2) Weekly Signal Review: Finance Ops performs a signal quality check and flags any L->P transitions to Finance Lead.
3) Trigger assessment meeting (ad-hoc, mandatory for Yellow/Red): Participants: Finance Lead, Head of Platform, Product Ops, Legal representative, Customer Success rep. Outcome: decision package with recommended operational mitigations and financial steps. Decision must include: expected cost delta, customer impact summary, communication plan, and timing.
4) Approval & execution: For Yellow triggers Finance Lead can approve procurement holds up to $250k incremental spend. For Red triggers, CFO sign-off required. Critical requires Executive review (CFO+CEO+Legal).

Procurement hold and release rules

- Hold actions (Yellow): Freeze new discretionary hardware purchases, suspend vendor onboarding for non-essential tools, pause multi-region expansion capacity purchases.
- Hold actions (Red): Pause all vendor purchases above $50k, halt planned headcount-backed MTAs for the affected function, and postpone annual license renewals that are non-critical.
- Release conditions: Holds are released when P signal returns to within +/- 5% for 30 days and C confirms the contract delta is <5% over 60 days. Release requires Finance Ops + Head of Procurement signoff.

Billing and revenue recognition coordination

When a trigger fires we must evaluate the impact on invoicing and revrec:

- If customer usage materially declines (P or C), update monthly billing forecasts and identify customers at risk for refunds or credits.
- RevRec policy adjustments: For Dedicated capacity contracts where we expect cancellations or downgrades, place a RevRec Review (owner: Accounting) to evaluate deferred revenue amortization changes and estimate churn-related recognition impacts.

Example: 30% reduction in RPM for a cohort of Dedicated customers

- Immediate steps: Finance Ops calculates the estimated MRR reduction and short-term cash impact; notify Accounting to run a revrec recalculation for deferred revenue.
- Accounting playbook excerpt (YAML):

  ---
  scenario: "dedicated-cohort-30pct-drop"
  estimate_window_days: 30
  action: "run_revrec_recalc"
  owner: "Accounting"
  notes: "prepare journal entries for deferred revenue adjustment and update forecast model with new churn curve"

Communication & CS routing

- Customer notifications: When mitigation impacts customers (throttling, model routing), CS & Account teams will send a templated notification within 24 hours. The template must include: reason, expected duration, alternatives, and contact for immediate escalations.
- Internal comms: A trigger bulletin in #finance-ops and #platform-ops summarizing the decision, mitigation steps, and owners.

Template: procurement hold notification (internal)

Subject: Procurement Hold - [Yellow|Red] Trigger - [date]
Body:
- Trigger: [L/P/C signals summary]
- Procurement actions: [list of freeze actions]
- Expected duration: [days]
- Required approvals: [names]
- Owner contact: [owner email]

Risk and legal considerations

- Contractual obligations: Legal must review any action that may alter customer SLAs or billing terms (owner: Legal). The playbook prohibits unilateral changes to customer-facing contract terms; any required change must follow Contract Amendment SOP and receive Legal + Sales Exec approval.
- Material adverse change (MAC): If a trigger indicates financial distress that could be considered a MAC under vendor or customer agreements, immediately escalate to Legal and Finance for assessment.

Operational mitigations catalogue (examples)

- Model routing fallback: Route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost, Redwood-verified variant.
- Aggressive caching: Increase prefix and KV cache retention for high-frequency endpoints.
- Batching & token limits: Apply dynamic batching heuristics and temporary token caps per request.
- Capacity burst gating: Use burst gating to keep baseline SLOs intact while blocking new long-running jobs.

Metrics and dashboards

Minimum dashboards required:
- Budget Signals dashboard (Finance Ops): RPM, tokens/call, revenue-weighted usage vs plan, committed capacity events.
- Procurement status board: Active PO values, pending approvals, vendor onboarding pipeline.
- RevRec impact dash: Deferred revenue, MRR movement, churn cohorts.

Appendices

A. Example SQL snippet (signal extraction):

SELECT date_trunc('day', timestamp) as day,
       sum(tokens) as tokens_day,
       count(distinct request_id) as calls_day,
       sum(billing_amount) as bill_day
FROM usage_events
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day DESC;

B. Example decision checklist for Yellow -> Red escalation:

- [ ] Confirm L and P exceed thresholds for 14 and 30 days respectively
- [ ] Validate data quality with Platform telemetry team
- [ ] Quantify cash impact and procurement exposure
- [ ] Draft customer impact communications and pre-approve with Legal
- [ ] Convene Trigger Assessment meeting and capture minutes

C. Ownership matrix (summary):

- Finance Ops: Signals ingestion, first-line analysis, procurement holds up to threshold
- Accounting: RevRec calculations and journal entries
- Head of Procurement: Execute holds and vendor communications
- Head of Platform: Implement operational mitigations and SLO tracking
- Legal: Contract assessment and amendment routing
- Customer Success: Customer notifications and remediation offers

Document maintenance

- Owner: Finance Ops (Maya Thompson)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or after any material MRR movement >10%
- Change log: All revisions must be recorded in the Confluence page history and reviewed by at least one Finance and one Product representative.
